examples.ko: 제 동생은 개그맨이 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a comedian.
That comedian's expressions are really funny.
I often see comedians on TV.
Everyone laughed loudly at the comedian's joke.
My friend took a photo with a comedian.

examples.ko: 저는 그 개그맨에게 사인을 받고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get that comedian's autograph.

explain: 여자 코미디언은 '개그우먼'이라고 해요. 영어 gag에서 온 '개그'와 man을 합친 한국식 외래어라서 영어 comedian 대신 한국에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: That female comedian has a really unique voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여자 코미디언을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a female comedian.

phrases.example: 저는 코미디언이 나오는 방송을 자주 봐요.
phrases.en: I often watch shows with comedians.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 다른 말이에요. 남녀 모두에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another word with the same meaning; used for any gender.

phrases.en: I'm going to become a comedian later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 '이/가 되다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '이/가 되다' when talking about dreams or jobs.

explain_en: A female comedian is a '개그우먼'. It is a Korean-made loanword combining 'gag' and 'man', used in Korea in place of English 'comedian'.

examples.en: Graduate students study in the lab until late at night.
My older brother is a graduate student, so he is very busy.
A new dormitory for graduate students has opened.
I asked a graduate student for Korean lessons.
I met my graduate student friend at the library.
I will become a graduate student next year.

explain: 대학교를 졸업한 뒤 더 깊이 공부하는 사람이에요. '대학생'과 달리 석사나 박사 과정을 공부해요. '대학원 다녀요'라고 말하는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: I attend graduate school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학원생이라는 말 대신 자기가 하는 일을 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to say you are a graduate student.

phrases.en: I will become a graduate student next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학원에 들어간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means entering graduate school.

phrases.example: 대학원생 선배가 공부 방법을 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: A senior grad student taught me how to study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학원에 먼저 들어온 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who entered graduate school earlier.

explain_en: This is someone who keeps studying after finishing university. Unlike a '대학생', they study in a master's or doctoral program. People also say '대학원 다녀요' (I attend grad school).

examples.en: My little girl starts school this year.
I bought a new bag for my daughter.

examples.ko: 딸내미는 요즘 그림에 푹 빠져 있어요.
examples.en: My daughter is really into drawing these days.
My daughter is already as tall as me.
I went to the market with my daughter.

examples.ko: 저 집 딸내미 정말 예쁘게 생겼네요.
examples.en: The girl from that house is really pretty.

explain: 부모나 이웃이 편하게 '딸'을 부르는 말이에요. 자기 딸이나 아는 집 딸에게 쓰고, 격식을 차릴 때는 '딸'이나 '따님'을 써요. 아들은 '아들내미'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My daughter loves books.
phrases.nuance_ko: '딸내미'보다 꾸밈없는 기본 말이라 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, neutral word that is safe to use with anyone, unlike the casual 딸내미.

phrases.en: The boss's daughter is getting married next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 딸을 높여 부르는 말이라 격식을 차릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to refer to someone else's daughter, used in polite situations.

phrases.en: My little girl sings really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 딸을 정답게 말할 때 '우리'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warm way to talk about your own daughter, often paired with '우리'.

explain_en: It is a casual way for parents or neighbors to say '딸'. It is used for your own daughter or a daughter you know, and in formal speech you use '딸' or '따님'. The word for son is '아들내미'.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 만화가가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to become a cartoonist since I was little.

examples.ko: 이 웹툰 만화가는 매주 새 이야기를 올려요.
examples.en: This webtoon cartoonist posts a new story every week.
I got an autograph from the cartoonist.
I saw a popular cartoonist's studio on TV.
They say making a living as a cartoonist isn't easy.

examples.ko: 동생은 만화가를 꿈꾸며 매일 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling dreams of being a cartoonist and draws every day.

explain: '-가'는 화가, 음악가, 소설가처럼 그 일을 직업으로 하는 사람 뒤에 붙어요. 웹툰을 그리는 사람은 '웹툰 작가'라고도 불러요. '만화가 재미있다'의 '만화+가(조사)'와 모양이 같으니 문장 속에서 구별해요.

phrases.example: 제 꿈은 웹툰 작가가 되는 거예요.
phrases.en: My dream is to become a webtoon artist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웹툰을 그리는 만화가를 말할 때 '만화가' 대신 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can replace '만화가' when talking about someone who draws webtoons.

phrases.example: 유명한 만화가를 직접 만나서 사인을 받았어요.
phrases.en: I met a famous cartoonist in person and got an autograph.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만화가' 앞에 꾸며 주는 말을 붙여 어떤 사람인지 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a describing word before '만화가' to say what kind of cartoonist.

phrases.en: My friend is a cartoonist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 소개할 때 쓰는 존댓말 서술형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite sentence ending used to state someone's job.

explain_en: The suffix '-가' attaches to people who do something as a profession, as in 화가, 음악가 and 소설가. Someone who draws webtoons is also called a '웹툰 작가'. It looks the same as '만화+가' (subject particle) in '만화가 재미있다', so tell them apart from context.

examples.en: My grandmother is a stylish person.

examples.ko: 그 멋쟁이 아저씨를 동네에서 다 알아요.
examples.en: Everyone in the neighborhood knows that stylish man.

examples.ko: 멋쟁이가 되려면 옷을 잘 맞춰 입어야 해요.
examples.en: To be stylish, you have to coordinate your clothes well.
You came out dressed up like a stylish person today.
My friend is stylish, so she works at a clothing shop.
Many stylish people gathered on the street.

explain: '-쟁이'는 어떤 특징이 있는 사람에게 붙는 말로 '욕심쟁이', '개구쟁이'도 있어요. 멋쟁이는 칭찬으로 써서 옷차림이 세련된 사람에게 말해요.

phrases.en: Your clothes are so nice today, you're really stylish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방에게 칭찬할 때 쓰는 존댓말 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to compliment someone directly.

phrases.example: 우리 반 멋쟁이 선생님은 늘 옷을 잘 입으세요.
phrases.en: Our stylish teacher always dresses well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 가리키는 말 앞에 붙여서 그 사람을 소개할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a word for a person to describe them as stylish.

phrases.en: With my new glasses, I became stylish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이 달라져서 세련된 사람이 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say someone became a stylish person after a change in looks.

explain_en: The ending -쟁이 attaches to a person with a certain trait, as in 욕심쟁이 and 개구쟁이. 멋쟁이 is a compliment for someone whose clothing looks refined.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 한국 방송에 처음 소개됐어요.
examples.en: That singer was first introduced on Korean TV.
This book is going to be introduced abroad too.
The new product is being featured in the news today.

examples.ko: 방송에 소개되는 식당마다 사람이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Every restaurant featured on TV gets lots of customers.

examples.ko: 우리 동네가 여행 잡지에 소개돼서 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm happy our neighborhood was featured in a travel magazine.

examples.ko: 영상으로 소개된 방법을 따라 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried the method introduced in the video.

explain: 방송, 책, 뉴스에서 어떤 사람이나 물건이 알려질 때 써요. 사람과 사람 사이에서는 '소개받다'가 더 자연스러워요. '친구에게 소개받았어요'처럼요. 내가 소개하면 '소개하다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 작은 식당이 TV 방송에 소개됐어요.
phrases.en: This small restaurant was featured on a TV show.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송에 나와서 사람들에게 알려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something appears on a broadcast and becomes known.

phrases.example: 한국 노래가 외국에 많이 소개되고 있어요.
phrases.en: Korean songs are being introduced abroad a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화나 물건이 다른 나라에 알려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when culture or products become known in other countries.

phrases.en: I bought a book that was featured in the news yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사 앞에서 어디에 나왔는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun tells where it was featured.

explain_en: It is used when a person or thing becomes known through TV, books, or news. Between people, 소개받다 is more natural, as in 친구에게 소개받았어요. When you introduce someone yourself, use 소개하다.

examples.ko: 시누이가 주말에 우리 집에 놀러 와요.
examples.en: My husband's sister is coming to visit our house on the weekend.
I get along quite well with my sister-in-law.
I was really grateful to get a gift from my sister-in-law.
My sister-in-law is getting married, so I prepared a gift of money.

examples.ko: 명절에는 시누이 가족이 다 같이 모여요.
examples.en: On holidays, my sister-in-law's family all gathers together.
I went to the market with my sister-in-law.

explain: 남편의 누나와 여동생을 모두 '시누이'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '시누이'라고 하지 않고, 손아래면 '아가씨', 손위면 '형님'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I have two sisters-in-law on my husband's side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 관계를 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when introducing family.

phrases.en: I went to my husband's sister's house on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '네'를 붙이면 그 사람의 집이나 가족을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 네 means that person's home or family.

phrases.en: I got a present from my husband's sister.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '한테'를 붙여 사람에게 받거나 주는 말을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle 한테 is used for giving to or getting from a person.
phrases.en_equiv: from or to the husband's sister

explain_en: Both a husband's older sister and younger sister are called 시누이. You don't address her as 시누이 directly; you call a younger one '아가씨' and an older one '형님'.

examples.ko: 동생은 장난감을 혼자 다 가지려는 욕심꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a greedy one who wants all the toys.
Like a greedy kid, I ate all the snacks by myself.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 욕심꾸러기라서 나눠 주지 않아요.
examples.en: My son is greedy, so he doesn't share.
I read a fairy tale with a greedy king.
Shall we talk about who the greedy one is?
Don't tease your friend by calling him greedy.

explain: '잠꾸러기', '장난꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'가 붙은 말로, 귀엽게 놀리는 말투로 아이에게 많이 써요. 어른에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. '욕심쟁이'와 거의 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: Don't eat it all by yourself like a greedy person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '욕심꾸러기'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 가볍게 놀리는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 욕심꾸러기, with a lightly teasing tone.

phrases.example: 동생은 욕심이 많아서 장난감을 안 빌려줘요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is greedy and won't lend out toys.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 부르는 말이 아니라 성격을 설명하는 중립적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral phrase that describes a trait rather than labeling a person.

phrases.en: Don't act greedy, share with your friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이에게 나누라고 말할 때 부드럽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to tell a child to share.

explain_en: Like '잠꾸러기' (sleepyhead) and '장난꾸러기' (prankster), '-꾸러기' makes a teasing but cute label, often used for children. Saying it directly to an adult can be rude. It's used almost the same as '욕심쟁이'.

examples.en: Our youngest is the well-known prankster of the family.

examples.ko: 장난꾸러기 동생 때문에 하루도 조용하지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of my mischievous younger sibling, no day is quiet.

examples.ko: 그 장난꾸러기가 또 선생님을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: That prankster surprised the teacher again.
They say a prankster still loves playing jokes after growing up.
Many people call me a prankster.

examples.ko: 장난꾸러기에게는 혼내기보다 일을 맡기는 게 좋대요.
examples.en: They say it's better to give a prankster a task than to scold them.

explain: '-꾸러기'는 그런 모습이 많은 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요. '잠꾸러기', '욕심꾸러기', '심술꾸러기'처럼 쓰고, 보통 귀엽게 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 어린아이에게 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 동생은 웃을 때 꼭 장난꾸러기 같아요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling looks like a little prankster when smiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같다'를 붙여 그런 느낌이 난다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 같다 says someone gives that impression.

phrases.example: 우리 집 장난꾸러기 강아지가 신발을 물어 갔어요.
phrases.en: Our mischievous puppy ran off with my shoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 귀여운 동물에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used not only for people but also for cute animals.

phrases.en: Thanks to our playful friend, the class is fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구를 귀엽게 놀리듯 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to fondly tease a friend.

explain_en: The ending -꾸러기 attaches to a person who shows a lot of that trait. It appears in 잠꾸러기, 욕심꾸러기 and 심술꾸러기, and it usually has a cute, teasing feel. It is used mostly for young children.

examples.en: My parents had an arranged marriage.

examples.ko: 중매결혼이라도 서로 사랑하며 사는 부부가 많아요.
examples.en: Even if it was an arranged marriage, many couples live lovingly together.
They say Grandma met Grandpa through an arranged marriage.

examples.ko: 연애결혼과 중매결혼 중에 뭐가 더 좋다고 생각해요?
examples.en: Which do you think is better, a love marriage or an arranged marriage?
I was curious how arranged marriages work, so I asked.
When the topic of arranged marriage came up, my mother smiled.

explain: '연애결혼'의 반대로 기억하면 좋아요. 중매는 사람을 소개해 주는 일이라서 '중매로 결혼했어요'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: They got married through a matchmaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중매결혼을 하다'를 풀어서 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A looser way of saying 'have an arranged marriage'.

phrases.en: The two of them met through a matchmaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼하기 전에 처음 만난 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how a couple first met.

phrases.en: I want a love marriage rather than an arranged marriage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중매결혼의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of an arranged marriage.

explain_en: It helps to remember it as the opposite of '연애결혼' (a love marriage). Matchmaking is introducing people to each other, so you can also say '중매로 결혼했어요'.

examples.en: A cowboy rides a horse and herds cattle.
Cowboys appear in Western movies.

examples.ko: 아이가 카우보이 모자를 쓰고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The child wore a cowboy hat and took a photo.
I watched a movie with a cowboy as the hero.
My uncle wears boots like a cowboy.
Even a cowboy gets tired after working all day.

explain: 영어 cowboy에서 온 외래어로, 미국 서부에서 말을 타고 소를 키우는 사람을 떠올리게 해요. '카우보이 모자', '카우보이 부츠'처럼 뒤에 다른 말을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 아버지가 카우보이 모자를 쓰고 사진을 찍었어요.
phrases.en: My father took a photo wearing a cowboy hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '카우보이' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙이면 그 사람이 쓰는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding an item name makes it that thing a cowboy wears.

phrases.example: 카우보이 부츠를 신으니까 키가 커 보여요.
phrases.en: I look taller wearing cowboy boots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자처럼 옷차림을 이야기할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another common pairing when talking about clothes.

phrases.en: I watched a cowboy movie on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서부 이야기를 다룬 영화를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a movie about the American West.

explain_en: A loanword from English 'cowboy', it calls to mind people on horseback raising cattle in the American West. It is often followed by another word: '카우보이 모자' (cowboy hat), '카우보이 부츠' (cowboy boots).

examples.en: The eldest son's wife has a lot to do during the holidays.
The eldest son's wife in our family is a good cook.
Grandmother trusts her eldest daughter-in-law the most.
She married in as the eldest son's wife and held the ancestral rites.
The whole family gathered for the eldest daughter-in-law's birthday.
The eldest and younger daughters-in-law get along well.

explain: 큰아들의 아내를 말하고, 짝말은 '작은며느리'(또는 '둘째 며느리')예요. 전통적으로 제사와 명절 일을 많이 맡는 자리라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The eldest son's wife is busy during holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: '큰며느리'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 전통적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 'keun-myeoneuri', a little more traditional.

phrases.example: 그분은 작년에 이 집의 큰며느리가 되었어요.
phrases.en: She became this family's eldest daughter-in-law last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰아들과 결혼해서 그 자리가 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when marrying the first son and taking that role.

phrases.en: We welcomed our eldest daughter-in-law last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시부모 입장에서 며느리를 맞이했다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the in-laws' side when gaining a daughter-in-law.

explain_en: It means the eldest son's wife, and the counterpart is '작은며느리' (or '둘째 며느리' for the second). Traditionally it carries a sense of the person who takes on much of the ancestral rites and holiday work.

examples.en: My eldest brother is ten years older than me.

examples.ko: 큰형이 회사에 다닌 지 오 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been five years since my eldest brother started working at a company.
When I was little, I learned Hangeul from my eldest brother.
On holidays the family gathers at my eldest brother's house.
I take after my eldest brother, so I am tall.
My eldest brother and I have similar hobbies.

explain: 남자가 자기 형을 부르는 말이 '형'이고, 여자는 '오빠'라고 해요. 형이 둘 이상이면 가장 위를 '큰형', 그다음은 '둘째 형'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 그냥 '형'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: My eldest brother always helps me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '님'을 붙여서 더 높이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '님' makes it more respectful.

phrases.en: I called my eldest brother on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한테'는 말할 때 '에게' 대신 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '한테' is used in speech instead of '에게'.

phrases.en: My eldest brother is good at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족을 말할 때는 '내' 대신 '우리'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For family, Koreans often say '우리' instead of 'my'.

explain_en: A man calls his older brother '형', while a woman says '오빠'. With two or more older brothers, the eldest is 큰형 and the next is '둘째 형'. When calling him directly, people usually just say '형'.
